rhs_for_integrator: Rmax * C / (Km * (Na0 / Na) + C) + Rmax2 * C**hill / (Km2**hill + C**hill) - Rleak * C / (Kleak + C) * (Na / (KNa + Na)) - Rmax * C / (Km * (Na0 / Na) + C) * (C**ninh / (Kinh**ninh + C**ninh))
sanity_expectations: At fixed Na, R rises steeply with C at low concentrations (carrier-mediated uptake)
R approaches a saturating plateau as transporters saturate
At high C the substrate-driven SGLT2 inhibition plus back-leak cause R to peak and then decline modestly (non-monotonic, not strictly increasing)
R is finite, real, and non-negative across the sampled region
Increasing Na raises apparent SGLT2 affinity (via Na0/Na) and increases the back-leak saturation factor Na/(KNa+Na)
excitation_report: σ=0.1, k=5 (Sobol, 512 samples over C∈[0.5,80], Na∈[80,160]). Per-term σ-multiples: SGLT2 saturable C*Rmax/(C+Km*Na0/Na)=91.9×; SGLT1 Hill=18.6×; back-leak (weakest)=5.85×; NEW substrate-inhibition -C*C**ninh*Rmax/((C+Km*Na0/Na)*(C**ninh+Kinh**ninh))=59.5×. New-term-vs-parent peak effect 8.55 (85.5×σ) at C≈79.9, Na≈113.9. No weak terms; auto_balance converged with no coefficient changes.
role_corrections: R: output->dependent variable (confirmed; explicitly solvable, on LHS)
C: input/axis->independent variable (confirmed; primary sampling axis, plasma glucose)
Na: input/axis->independent variable (confirmed; sampled 80-160 mM to keep the Na0/Na affinity-shift and Na/(KNa+Na) back-leak terms identifiable)
Na0: parameter (confirmed, fixed 140 mM reference sodium)
Kinh: parameter (confirmed, fixed 30 mM, within suggested 20-60)
rationale: Explicit algebraic saturation/inhibition relation for renal glucose reabsorption; R is directly evaluable from C and Na. C is the primary axis (0.5-80 mM), extended into the hyperglycemic range so the new substrate-driven inhibition term (Kinh=30) is strongly excited. Na is sampled (80-160 mM around Na0=140) to keep both sodium-dependent terms identifiable rather than folded into rescaled constants. Parameters use physiologically-inspired magnitudes (SGLT2 Km~2 mM, SGLT1 lower affinity, minor back-leak); auto_balance and excitation_check confirmed all four terms exceed 5σ with no coefficient changes needed.

scenario_text: A study of renal glucose handling measures the rate at which the kidney reabsorbs glucose from filtrate as plasma glucose concentration rises. Transport is carrier-mediated, so reabsorption climbs steeply at low concentrations and then plateaus as transporters saturate. Conditions are held at steady filtration. We measure tubular glucose reabsorption rate against plasma glucose concentration.
